clue.text: Port one point short of Paradise

parts.note: paradise is another name for heaven
E (east) is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A harbour that falls just one step short of being heaven on earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' takes E (east, one point of the compass) out of HEAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven is a harbour or anchorage where ships shelter, which is what a port is.

clue.text: Dickensian character seen in a churchyard

definitions.meaning: Bradley ... is the murderous schoolmaster in Dickens's Our Mutual Friend
a memorial slab at the head of a grave

explanation.surface: A figure from Dickens spotted among the graves.
explanation.definitionFit: Bradley Headstone is a Dickens villain, and the upright stone marking a grave stands in every churchyard.

clue.text: One showing preference by bestowing a kiss?

definitions.text: One showing preference by bestowing a kiss?

parts.words: One showing preference by bestowing a kiss?
parts.note: the kiss is the X written on a ballot paper beside the chosen candidate

explanation.surface: Someone who shows whom they favour with a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: At an election a person marks a cross, the X also used for a kiss, against the candidate preferred.

clue.text: Nodding off to sound of hammering

indicators.note: the sound of a word is what it is like when spoken, so the hammering word is heard rather than read

parts.note: knapping is chipping flints by striking them with a hammer

explanation.surface: Dozing off to the noise of someone hammering.
explanation.walkthrough: KNAPPING, with its silent K, is said just like NAPPING.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a short sleep, dozing, is the same as dropping off to sleep.

clue.text: Plot to extend blanket protection

parts.note: a plot of garden ground is a bed
to extend is to spread

explanation.surface: Advice to enlarge a plot, or a policy of protecting everything at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blanket protection' reads as cover for everything; here it is literal, the cover laid over the blankets.
explanation.definitionFit: This top cover lies over the bed's blankets and keeps them clean, so it literally protects them.

clue.text: Three-quarters run away, retiring to left-wing

indicators.note: three of four letters are kept, so the last quarter of the word goes

parts.note: to bolt is to run away
retiring means shy, reserved

explanation.surface: Rugby backs scarpering and then backing off towards the left wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three-quarters' keeps BOL of BOLT. In rugby the three-quarters are backs who play on the wings, which drives the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshy is British slang, from Bolshevik, for having rebellious or radical left-wing attitudes.

clue.text: Sort of shop under no obligation

definitions.meaning: an airport shop selling goods without tax

explanation.surface: A kind of shop where nothing is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Airport shops sell goods without tax, and the phrase literally means free from any duty or obligation.

clue.text: Fish cake

definitions.meaning: an edible fish of the Indian and Pacific oceans
a ... cake is a small liquorice sweet from Pontefract in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A fishcake.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR joined the printed 'Fish cake' into one word. Pontefract cakes, also called Pomfret cakes, are small black liquorice discs.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a food fish and the liquorice disc made at Pontefract, Pomfret being the town's old name.

clue.text: Cautioned form in the process of imparting knowledge

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so the letters of the first word are shaped into something new

explanation.surface: Being warned while being taught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges CAUTIONED.
explanation.definitionFit: Teaching and schooling are the process of passing on knowledge.

clue.text: Sundry adventures include being in the woods

indicators.note: the phrase includes the answer, spread across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Various escapades taking place among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across sunDRY ADventures.
explanation.definitionFit: A dryad is a tree nymph of Greek myth, a spirit living in the forest.

explanation.surface: A plain person likened to the cartoon cat's rival.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousy means drab and timid, and also literally mouse-like, as Jerry of Tom and Jerry is.

clue.text: Orthodox footballer playing the game

parts.note: conventional or orthodox means straight
a forward is an attacking footballer

explanation.surface: A conventional footballer taking part in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing the game' looks like the footballer in action; it is the idiom for acting honestly and fairly.
explanation.definitionFit: To play the game is an idiom for behaving honestly and fairly, which is being frank and direct.

clue.text: Princely House colour

definitions.meaning: the House of ...-Nassau is the Dutch royal dynasty, once princes of the town of ...
a hue between red and yellow

explanation.surface: The colour associated with a royal dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch royal family is the House of Orange, and the same word names a reddish-yellow hue.

clue.text: New drama done for the stars

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A fresh play staged for the celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges DRAMA DONE. 'Stars' looks like actors; it is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation, a named group of stars in the northern sky.

clue.text: Young and in a comfortable position

definitions.meaning: a baby bird still in the nest; young as a noun means offspring
settled snugly, as when curling up cosily

explanation.surface: Someone youthful who is sitting comfortably.
explanation.definitionFit: A chick not yet fledged is a nestling, and nestling also means snuggling cosily into place.

clue.text: Fighter sounds like a tough guy

indicators.note: this tells the solver the word for a tough guy is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a gorilla is slang for a thug or heavy

explanation.surface: A fighter who resembles a hard man.
explanation.walkthrough: GORILLA and GUERRILLA are said the same way. The scan shows the count (9) the held clue lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla is an irregular combatant in a small independent band.

clue.text: Standard source of colours in the wars

definitions.meaning: a standard is a shrub trained onto a single upright stem, as roses often are

definitions.text: source of colours in the wars
definitions.meaning: the red and white roses were the badges of York and Lancaster in the Wars of the Roses

explanation.surface: A flag that supplied the colours in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' and 'colours' both suggest military flags. The Wars of the Roses were the 15th-century English civil wars between York and Lancaster, each with a rose badge.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub grown on one tall stem is a standard; the plant gave the red and white flower emblems of the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Deny moon is involved? Not so — he's a handsome boy!

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of these words are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letter pool
taken as written, part of the letter pool
taken as written, part of the letter pool
these letters are to be removed from the pool, as 'Not so' says

explanation.surface: A denial that the moon has anything to do with him, since he is a beautiful youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' mixes DENY MOON IS, and 'Not so' takes S and O out of the pool. A neat touch: in Greek myth this youth was loved by Selene, the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Endymion was a beautiful shepherd whom the moon goddess Selene loved, so he is the archetype of male beauty.

clue.text: It deadens the sound for carol singers in winter

definitions.meaning: a silencer that damps noise, as on an exhaust
a warm scarf worn round the neck outdoors

explanation.surface: Something that dampens the noise made by Christmas carollers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests muting the singers; the second sense is the scarf they wrap up in.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffler is an exhaust silencer, and also a thick scarf worn by people out in the cold.

clue.text: Fortune for a part of church without money

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: the chancel is the part of a church around the altar
L stands for the pound, from Latin libra, so it means money

explanation.surface: Luck or fate attending part of a church that has no funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes L (pound, money) from CHANCEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Chance means luck or fortune, the unpredictable way events fall out.

clue.text: Crown collection for benefit of listeners

parts.note: the crown is the top of the head
a set is a collection of things

explanation.surface: A crown and a set of jewels shown off for an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown' looks like regalia; it means the top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Earphones joined by a band let a person hear sound privately, so they serve the listener.

clue.text: Wisdom of Egyptian god hoarding copper

indicators.note: hoarding means storing away, so the god's name holds the metal inside it

parts.note: Amen, also spelt Amun, is the Egyptian king of the gods
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: An ancient deity's sagacity while he stockpiles metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is shrewdness and sharp judgement, a practical kind of good sense.

clue.text: Produce a lot of Gruyere with cha and coffee for the old writer

indicators.note: to produce is to make something out of materials, so these letters are reworked
most but not all of the cheese's name, so its last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe of cheese, tea and coffee for a writer of long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the last E of GRUYERE, leaving GRUYER; 'Produce' rearranges GRUYER, CHA and COFFEE. Cha is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer, author of The Canterbury Tales in the fourteenth century, is the classic old English poet.

clue.text: Greely's advice on Poles' habits

parts.note: Horace Greeley, the US newspaper editor, is famed for the advice 'Go West, young man', and W is west
the north and south poles give N and S

explanation.surface: An American editor's tips on what people from Poland wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR misread the printed 'Greely's'; the setter spells Greeley without its second E. 'Poles' looks like the nationality, but means the earth's poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a long robe, as worn by monks or nuns, so habits are gowns.

clue.text: Hiding place for a docked seal

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a cachet is a seal stamped on a letter or document

explanation.surface: A secret spot for a seal that has had its tail cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' cuts the final T of CACHET. 'Seal' looks like the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a secret store of things put away out of sight.

clue.text: Maybe Catherine will take a turn?

definitions.text: Maybe Catherine will take a turn?

parts.words: Maybe Catherine will take a turn?
parts.note: Catherine looks like a woman taking her turn; it is the spinning firework named after Saint Catherine, whose instrument of martyrdom also turns

explanation.walkthrough: A Catherine wheel is a spinning firework, named after the saint who was to be broken on a spiked wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catherine wheel is a firework, and the round thing that turns on an axle is the device the saint was martyred on.

clue.text: Not with it when it comes to scoring

definitions.text: Not with it when it comes to scoring

parts.words: Not with it when it comes to scoring

explanation.definitionFit: Lacking musical talent means having no gift for scores, the written form of music.

clue.text: Baker Street Irregular in Neptune's domain?

definitions.text: Baker Street Irregular in Neptune's domain?

parts.words: Baker Street Irregular in Neptune's domain?
parts.note: the Baker Street Irregulars were the street boys who helped Sherlock Holmes; one of them under the waves would be a spiny marine creature

explanation.surface: One of Sherlock Holmes's young helpers adrift in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: Neptune is the Roman god of the ocean. A street urchin is a ragged child; the sea creature shares the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny echinoderm is named after the hedgehog, once called an urchin, and lives in the ocean ruled by Neptune.

clue.text: Volunteers show character

definitions.meaning: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve, is ..., so the phrase reads as one name for them
a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Volunteer soldiers proving their mettle.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve; 'show' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth Greek letter is theta, and a letter is a written character; split, the word is also the volunteer reserve's name.
